 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. In this story The action in No. 2 Georgia's 42-7 blowout win over No. 10 Ole Miss was halted with about five minutes to go before halftime on Saturday night.
 The Bulldogs were driving when Ole Miss defensive back Jaylon Braxton was called for defensive pass interference on Craig Dandridge, who was tracking a deep pass from Georgia quarterback Gunner Stockton.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement It didn't look like anything happened in real time, but on the replay, Braxton grabs Dandridge's left arm.
 Fans disagreed with the call. After boos rained down from the stands, trash followed. The Dawgs were driving toward the Rebels' student section, and students tossed trash into the end zone as officers and staff cleaned up the mess.
 Overall, the game was delayed about six minutes, requiring repeated PA announcements and a message on the video board.
 At the time of the delay, Georgia was leading 21-0. Ole Miss fans were clearly frustrated by how the game had gone to that point, and the DPI call pushed them over the edge.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement After play resumed, Stockton ran in a 15-yard touchdown to take the early 28-0 lead.
 When the dust settled, the Bulldogs solidified the 35-point victory. Stockton only completed nine passes, but they went for 186 yards and four touchdowns. He also added 28 yards and scored on the ground.
 Georgia wide receiver Talyn Taylor had a huge game. Taylor finished with 140 yards and three touchdowns on four receptions.
 The Bulldogs return home next weekend and host No. 18 Missouri. Georgia is expected to take over as the No. 1 team in next week's CFP rankings after No. 1 Miami fell to No. 11 Notre Dame , 31-24.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Ole Miss goes on the road next week to face Oklahoma. This is the Rebels' third loss of the season, and it will be interesting to see how far the committee drops them for this performance.
 Quarterback Trinidad Chambliss finished 18 of 34 passing for 170 yards with an interception. Chambliss also had nine rushes for -12 yards as the Georgia defense consistently tackled him for a loss in the backfield.
 Running back Shekai Mills-Knight scored the Rebels' lone touchdown on an 8-yard rush early in the fourth quarter.
